[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Pandas DataFrames and Data Manipulation in Python"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Pandas is a powerful Python library for data analysis and manipulation. At its core is the DataFrame, a two-dimensional labeled data structure with columns of potentially different types. This tutorial will guide you through creating, manipulating, and analyzing DataFrames."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating DataFrames"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"DataFrames can be created from various sources, including dictionaries, lists, NumPy arrays, and external files (CSV, Excel, SQL databases)."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"# Creating a DataFrame from a dictionary
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Name': ['Alice', 'Bob', 'Charlie', 'David'],
    'Age': [25, 30, 27, 22],
    'City': ['New York', 'London', 'Paris', 'Tokyo']
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
print(df)"},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"# Creating a DataFrame from a list of lists
data = [
    ['Alice', 25, 'New York'],
    ['Bob', 30, 'London'],
    ['Charlie', 27, 'Paris'],
    ['David', 22, 'Tokyo']
]

df = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=['Name', 'Age', 'City'])
print(df)"},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Accessing Data"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can access data in a DataFrame using various methods, including column names, row indices (loc), and integer indices (iloc)."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"# Accessing a column
print(df['Name'])

# Accessing a row by label (index)
print(df.loc[0])

# Accessing a row by integer position
print(df.iloc[0])

# Accessing a specific element
print(df.loc[0, 'Name'])
print(df.iloc[0, 0])"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Data Manipulation"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Pandas provides a wide range of functions for data manipulation, including filtering, sorting, adding/removing columns, and grouping."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"# Filtering data
filtered_df = df[df['Age'] > 25]
print(filtered_df)

# Sorting data
sorted_df = df.sort_values(by='Age', ascending=False)
print(sorted_df)

# Adding a new column
df['Salary'] = [60000, 70000, 65000, 55000]
print(df)

# Removing a column
df = df.drop('City', axis=1)
print(df)"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Grouping and Aggregation"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Grouping allows you to group rows based on one or more columns and then apply aggregation functions (e.g., sum, mean, count) to each group."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"# Grouping by a column and calculating the mean
grouped_df = df.groupby('Age')['Salary'].mean()
print(grouped_df)

# Multiple aggregations
agg_df = df.groupby('Age').agg({'Salary': ['mean', 'sum'], 'Name': 'count'})
print(agg_df)"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Handling Missing Data"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Pandas provides functions to identify and handle missing data (NaN values)."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"# Creating a DataFrame with missing values
import numpy as np

data = {
    'Name': ['Alice', 'Bob', 'Charlie', 'David'],
    'Age': [25, 30, np.nan, 22],
    'City': ['New York', None, 'Paris', 'Tokyo']
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Checking for missing values
print(df.isnull())

# Filling missing values
df['Age'].fillna(df['Age'].mean(), inplace=True)
df['City'].fillna('Unknown', inplace=True)
print(df)"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Reading and Writing Data"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Pandas can read data from and write data to various file formats."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"# Reading from a CSV file
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Writing to a CSV file
df.to_csv('output.csv', index=False)

# Reading from an Excel file
df = pd.read_excel('data.xlsx')

# Writing to an Excel file
df.to_excel('output.xlsx', index=False)"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a basic introduction to Pandas DataFrames and data manipulation. Explore the Pandas documentation for more advanced features and functionalities."}]
